title: Classical Philosophy — Foundations
description: A survey of Western philosophy from its origins in 6th-century Greece through the Hellenistic schools of Rome. Students read primary texts — Plato, Aristotle, Epictetus, Epicurus — and engage directly with the questions these thinkers posed: What is the world made of? What can we know? What makes a life worth living? How should we face death? No prior philosophy background required.
learning_outcomes: Identify the core philosophical questions posed by the Pre-Socratics and explain why they matter
Analyze the Socratic method and apply it to test a knowledge claim
Explain Plato's Theory of Forms and the three Republic analogies (Cave, Sun, Divided Line)
Describe Aristotle's account of eudaimonia and the role of virtue and habit in achieving it
Distinguish the Stoic and Epicurean approaches to achieving tranquility and facing death
Construct a structured philosophical argument using only primary texts from the course
Read pre-modern philosophical prose accurately and respond critically in writing
